legitimate_personal_agent_use.finding: house hunting for one person (searching, saving homes, requesting a tour the user approved) is personal use. TechCrunch (2026-10-06) reports Zillow said it allows artificial intelligence agents acting on behalf of consumers; that statement was not seen in Zillow's own words.

peer_operator_risk.finding: Zillow refused an automated fetch of its own terms page (HTTP 403, 2026-10-11), so it runs bot defenses that may flag residential peers carrying agent traffic, and a flagged operator could lose access to Zillow for their own use.

site_position.finding: the public statement is supportive, but the terms as quoted by a secondary source say that without a commercial agreement the services may be used only for transactions on your own behalf, and acting for someone needs proof of authorization. the primary terms page was not read; this finding is unverified until the reviewer reads it by hand.

recommendation.rationale: defer: the statement is the most welcoming of the three, but the terms were not read at the primary source. before any approval: read the primary terms by hand, and ask Zillow to confirm in writing that a user's own agent counts as the user acting on their own behalf.
